lessons.title: Types of Metals: Steel, Aluminum, and Alloys
lessons.body: In metal packaging, the three main materials you will work with are steel, aluminum, and their alloys. Steel is strong and cheap, made from iron and carbon. Tinplate is steel coated with a thin layer of tin to stop rust. It is used for food cans, paint tins, and bottle caps. Tin-free steel (TFS) uses chromium instead of tin; it is cheaper and good for beer and beverage cans. Aluminum is lightweight, does not rust, and conducts heat well. It is perfect for drink cans, aerosol cans, and foil trays. Alloys mix metals to improve properties. For example, aluminum 3004 is used for can bodies because it is strong and easy to shape. In Africa, you can source steel from local scrap or import from South Africa, Egypt, or Nigeria. Aluminum is recycled locally in many countries. When choosing, consider cost, corrosion resistance, and weight. Steel is heavier but cheaper; aluminum is lighter but costs more. For food, use tinplate or coated steel. For drinks, aluminum is best. Always check the metal grade: for cans, look for 'tinplate' or 'aluminum 3004'. Test with a magnet: steel sticks, aluminum does not. This simple test helps you sort metals at the workshop.

lessons.title: Can Manufacturing: Two-Piece and Three-Piece
lessons.body: Can manufacturing has two main methods: two-piece and three-piece. In three-piece cans, you make a body by rolling a rectangular sheet into a cylinder and welding the side seam. Then you attach a top and bottom end. This is common for food cans like tomato paste or corned beef. The body is usually tinplate, and the ends are also tinplate. The weld is done with a copper wire electrode; you must control the current to avoid burn-through. In two-piece cans, you start with a circular blank of aluminum or steel. A press draws it into a cup, then a second draw stretches it into a tall can. There is no side seam, so no leaks. This is how beverage cans are made. The bottom is formed in the same piece. The top end is seamed on later. For a small-scale operation in Africa, three-piece can making is more practical because you can use a manual roller and a spot welder. Two-piece requires expensive deep-drawing presses. However, you can buy pre-formed two-piece cans and fill them. Key tools: sheet metal shears, roller, welder, seamer. For three-piece, cut body blanks to size, roll into cylinder, weld seam, then flange both ends. For two-piece, you need a press. Always test for leaks by filling with water and checking for drips. In Africa, many small canneries use imported two-piece cans and focus on filling and seaming.

lessons.title: Coating and Lining Technologies
lessons.body: Metal cans need a coating or lining to protect the food or drink from the metal, and to protect the metal from acids. Without a lining, acidic foods like tomatoes or pineapple will react with the tinplate, causing off-flavors and rust. The most common linings are epoxy, phenolic, and acrylic. Epoxy is used for acidic foods and beverages. Phenolic is for meats and fish. Acrylic is for beer and some fruits. You can apply linings by spraying, roller coating, or electrocoating. In small workshops, spray coating is easiest. First, clean the metal with a solvent like acetone. Then spray a thin, even coat of food-grade epoxy. Cure it in an oven at 200Â°C for 10-15 minutes. The coating must be 5-10 microns thick. Too thin, it fails; too thick, it cracks. For cans, you also need to coat the seams and ends. Always use food-safe coatings that meet FDA or equivalent standards. In Africa, you can buy epoxy resin from chemical suppliers in Kenya, Nigeria, or South Africa. Test the coating by filling the can with a saltwater solution and leaving it for 48 hours. If you see rust or blisters, the coating is bad. Also, check for pinholes by holding the can up to a light. A good lining is smooth and shiny, with no gaps.

lessons.title: Ends, Easy-Open Ends, and Seaming
lessons.body: Can ends are critical for sealing and opening. There are two main types: standard ends and easy-open ends (EOE). Standard ends require a can opener. Easy-open ends have a scored line and a tab that you pull to open. The tab is riveted to the end. To make an EOE, you start with a coated aluminum or tinplate sheet. You stamp out a circular blank, then form the curl and the countersink. The score line is made with a sharp die that cuts partway through the metal. The tab is made from a separate piece and attached with a rivet. For small-scale production, you can buy pre-made EOEs and seam them onto your cans. Seaming is the process of attaching the end to the can body. You use a seaming chuck and rolls. The end is placed on the can, then the first operation roll curls the edge of the end around the can flange. The second operation roll tightens the seam. The seam must be airtight and leak-proof. A good seam has a thickness of about 1.2 mm and a width of 2.5 mm. You can check with a seam micrometer. In Africa, manual seaming machines are available for small canneries. Always test seams by immersing filled cans in hot water (80Â°C) for 5 minutes and looking for bubbles. If bubbles appear, the seam is bad. Adjust the rolls and try again.

lessons.title: Aerosol and Specialty Metal Packaging
lessons.body: Aerosol cans are used for products like insect spray, paint, deodorant, and cooking spray. They are made of tinplate or aluminum. The can must withstand internal pressure of 3-6 bar. Aerosol cans have a concave bottom for strength and a valve on top. The valve is crimped onto the can. The propellant is a gas like butane or propane, mixed with the product. For small-scale production in Africa, you can buy empty aerosol cans and a filling machine. The filling process: first, the product is put into the can, then the valve is crimped, then the propellant is injected through the valve. You need a pressure tester to check for leaks. Specialty metal packaging includes tubes for toothpaste or ointments, trays for food, and drums for chemicals. Aluminum tubes are made by impact extrusion: a slug of aluminum is punched into a die to form a tube. The tube is then coated inside and outside. For drums, steel is rolled and welded. In Africa, metal drums are often reconditioned and reused for chemicals or water. Always check for corrosion and clean thoroughly. For aerosols, safety is key: never fill near a flame, and use proper ventilation. Test every batch for pressure and leaks. A simple soap bubble test can find leaks: spray soapy water on the valve and look for bubbles.

lessons.title: Corrosion and Compatibility Testing
lessons.body: Corrosion is the enemy of metal packaging. It happens when metal reacts with oxygen, water, or acids. For food and drinks, you must test that the product does not corrode the can and that the can does not spoil the product. Common tests include: salt spray test (ASTM B117), which exposes the can to a salt mist for 24-72 hours to see if rust forms. For compatibility, you fill the can with the actual product and store it at 40Â°C for 3 months. Then you check for off-flavors, color changes, and metal dissolution. You can also do a simple test: fill the can with the product, seal it, and leave it at room temperature for 2 weeks. Open it and look for rust, pitting, or a metallic taste. For acidic products like tomato sauce, use a coated can. For salty products, use tinplate with a lacquer. In Africa, you can do a basic corrosion test by burying a can in wet soil for a week; if it rusts, the coating is poor. Always keep records of your tests. If a can fails, check the coating thickness, the seam, and the metal grade. A good can should last at least 2 years on the shelf. Remember: corrosion is faster in hot, humid climates, so store cans in a cool, dry place. Test each new batch of cans and each new product formula.

quiz.q: Which metal is lightweight, does not rust, and is commonly used for drink cans?
quiz.explanation: Aluminum is lightweight, corrosion-resistant, and ideal for beverage cans.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between two-piece and three-piece cans?
options: A) Two-piece cans have a side seam, three-piece do not
B) Three-piece cans are made by deep drawing, two-piece by welding
C) Two-piece cans have no side seam, three-piece have a welded side seam
D) Three-piece cans are only for aerosols
quiz.explanation: Two-piece cans are drawn from a single piece of metal, so no side seam; three-piece cans have a welded body seam.

quiz.q: Which coating is best for acidic foods like tomato sauce?
quiz.explanation: Epoxy linings resist acids and are commonly used for acidic foods and beverages.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of an easy-open end?
options: A) To make the can stronger
B) To allow opening without a can opener
quiz.explanation: Easy-open ends have a tab and score line so consumers can open the can by hand.

quiz.q: What internal pressure must an aerosol can withstand?
quiz.explanation: Aerosol cans typically hold 3-6 bar of pressure from propellants.

quiz.q: Which test is used to check corrosion resistance of a can?
quiz.explanation: The salt spray test exposes cans to a salt mist to accelerate corrosion and evaluate resistance.

quiz.q: What simple test can distinguish steel from aluminum?
quiz.explanation: A magnet sticks to steel but not to aluminum.

quiz.q: In three-piece can manufacturing, what joins the body seam?
quiz.explanation: The side seam of a three-piece can is welded using an electric welder.

quiz.q: What is the typical curing temperature for epoxy can lining?
quiz.explanation: Epoxy linings are usually cured at around 200Â°C for 10-15 minutes.

quiz.q: What is the function of a seaming roll in canning?
options: A) To cut the can body
B) To curl the end onto the can flange
quiz.explanation: Seaming rolls curl and tighten the end onto the can body to form a leak-proof seal.

quiz.q: Which metal is commonly used for aerosol cans?
quiz.explanation: Aerosol cans are made from tinplate or aluminum due to their strength and corrosion resistance.

quiz.q: What is a common defect in can lining?
quiz.explanation: Pinholes are small holes in the coating that allow corrosion; they are a common defect.

quiz.q: Why is a concave bottom used on aerosol cans?
options: B) To increase strength against pressure
C) To make it easier to open
quiz.explanation: The concave shape adds strength to withstand internal pressure.

quiz.q: What is the recommended storage condition to slow corrosion of metal cans?
quiz.explanation: Cool, dry conditions slow down the corrosion process.

quiz.q: Which alloy is commonly used for can bodies because it is strong and formable?
quiz.explanation: Aluminum 3004 is a common alloy for can bodies due to its strength and formability.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a score line on an easy-open end?
options: A) To make the can stronger
B) To allow the metal to tear open
quiz.explanation: The score line is a weakened line that tears when the tab is pulled.

quiz.q: What is the typical thickness of a good can seam?
quiz.explanation: A properly formed seam is about 1.2 mm thick for standard cans.

quiz.q: Which test can check for leaks in a seamed can?
quiz.explanation: Immersing filled cans in hot water (80Â°C) and looking for bubbles reveals leaks.

quiz.q: What is impact extrusion used to make?
quiz.explanation: Impact extrusion forms aluminum slugs into tubes for toothpaste or ointments.

quiz.q: Why is a lining needed in a metal can?
options: B) To prevent reaction between metal and product
quiz.explanation: The lining acts as a barrier to prevent the product from contacting and reacting with the metal.

quiz.q: What is the first step in making a three-piece can?
options: B) Rolling the body into a cylinder
quiz.explanation: The body is first rolled from a flat sheet into a cylinder, then welded.

quiz.q: Which of these is a specialty metal package?
quiz.explanation: Aluminum trays are a specialty metal packaging used for food.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a salt spray test?
quiz.explanation: Salt spray test accelerates corrosion to evaluate the protective coating's performance.

quiz.q: What is a common propellant used in aerosol cans?
quiz.explanation: Butane is a common propellant in aerosol products.

quiz.q: What does a seam micrometer measure?
quiz.explanation: A seam micrometer measures the thickness of the can seam to ensure it meets specifications.

quiz.q: Which coating is typically used for beer cans?
quiz.explanation: Acrylic coatings are often used for beer because they do not affect taste.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of two-piece cans over three-piece?
options: B) No side seam, so less leak risk
D) Can be made from steel only
quiz.explanation: Two-piece cans have no side seam, reducing the risk of leaks.

quiz.q: What is a common method for applying lining to small batches of cans?
quiz.explanation: Spray coating is practical for small-scale operations.

quiz.q: Why should you test a new can with the actual product?
options: B) To ensure compatibility and shelf life
quiz.explanation: Compatibility testing ensures the product does not react with the can and remains safe.

quiz.q: What is the first step in cleaning metal before coating?
quiz.explanation: Solvent cleaning removes oil and dirt to ensure proper coating adhesion.
